condition: Pleuritic chest pain, PE excluded clinically (PERC negative)
summary: 28-year-old man with right pleuritic chest pain after a week of coughing; HR 84, SpO₂ 98 %, no risk factors — low clinical probability and PERC negative.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Sharp right chest pain when breathing
inputs.hpi: One week of a dry cough after a cold, now sharp right lower chest pain on deep breathing and coughing for 2 days. Not breathless. No leg swelling, no recent surgery, travel, hormone use or previous clots. No haemoptysis.

exam.respiratory: Tender over the right 8th rib costochondral area reproducing the pain. Chest clear.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Musculoskeletal chest wall pain after viral cough
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Pleuritic chest wall pain after a viral cough. Low clinical probability of PE and PERC negative — no D-dimer or CTPA needed.

emergencyLevel.knownGapNote: Over-triage from negation: 'Not breathless' matches the post-operative/breathless rule and 'No haemoptysis' the haemoptysis rule (both urgent) → emergency_now for a PERC-negative patient.

mustExclude.note: PERC negative in a low-probability patient: no further PE testing.

guideline.name: Pulmonary Embolism Rule-out Criteria (PERC)
guideline.section: In low pre-test probability only: age <50, HR <100, SpO₂ ≥95%, no haemoptysis, no oestrogen use, no prior VTE, no unilateral leg swelling, no surgery/trauma requiring hospitalisation within 4 weeks — all negative → no further testing
guideline.citation: Kline JA, Mitchell AM, Kabrhel C, Richman PB, Courtney DM. Clinical criteria to prevent unnecessary diagnostic testing in emergency department patients with suspected pulmonary embolism. J Thromb Haemost. 2004;2:1247–55.

guideline.name: NICE NG158 — Venous thromboembolic diseases: diagnosis, management and thrombophilia testing
guideline.section: DVT: two-level Wells; likely (≥2) → proximal leg vein ultrasound within 4 h (interim anticoagulation and D-dimer if delayed); unlikely → D-dimer. PE: two-level Wells; likely (>4) → CTPA immediately (interim anticoagulation if delayed); unlikely (≤4) → D-dimer; PERC may be used when pre-test probability is low
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Venous thromboembolic diseases: diagnosis, management and thrombophilia testing (NG158). London: NICE; 2020 (updated 2023).

rationale: Permutation: the opposite end — low pre-test probability with all eight PERC criteria negative. Tests over-investigation (CTPA with radiation and contrast) and over-triage.
